name: Dragon Hotel Garden Restaurant
why_it_matters: The Skyabu family's guesthouse on the edge of the old village — five minutes' walk from Yuru Gompa. The garden restaurant cooks Ladakhi and Indian dishes from ingredients grown in their own kitchen plot, including apricots and walnuts.
insider_tip: Eat in the open-air garden if the weather holds — the dining room is fine but the garden is the reason to come. Order the apple juice over the soft drinks; it's pressed locally.
signature_address: Old Village edge, Lamayuru 194106, Leh District, Ladakh

name: Hotel Moonland Restaurant
why_it_matters: Hillside hotel built in the late 2010s with a restaurant terrace that frames Yuru Gompa from the same angle as the postcards. Sister property of Grand Moonland; the kitchen runs the widest menu in the village — Ladakhi staples plus an unexpected pizza-and-pancake line for the Srinagar–Leh overnight crowd.
insider_tip: Reviewers single out the momos — order them and skip the continental pretensions. Lunch service is faster than dinner because tour buses fill the dining room from 7pm.
signature_address: Leh-Kargil Highway, Lamayuru 194106, Leh District, Ladakh

name: Hotel Niranjana Restaurant
why_it_matters: The hotel directly adjacent to Lamayuru Monastery — locals call it the de facto monastery guesthouse. Run by a retired military officer; the basement restaurant is the closest sit-down meal to Yuru Gompa's morning prayers.
insider_tip: Stay over to catch the 6am monastery chants — the kitchen serves an early breakfast for guests heading to prayers. Cash only; no ATMs in the village.
signature_address: Near Lamayuru Monastery, Lamayuru 194101, Leh District, Ladakh

name: Lion's Den Guest House Restaurant
why_it_matters: Konchok Gyalsan's family guesthouse, opened 2010, two minutes' walk from the monastery. Restaurant is built in traditional Ladakhi style with low cushioned seating, and the kitchen runs strictly pure-veg and organic — most produce comes from the family's own plot. The room of choice for travellers wanting an actual Ladakhi meal, not a tourist-menu approximation.
insider_tip: Skyu — the local pasta-and-vegetable stew — is on the menu only by request; ask the day before. The rooftop suite gets the Moonland view at sunset.
